Interface Economics: Handoff Cost Models [M/S · unmetered]

Unmetered microeconomic & channel-coding model extending Coase (1937), Williamson (1979) & Marschak-Radner (1972) to software/agent APIs: typed gates win when spec + gate cost beats downstream error loss.

1/2 Amortization vs exploration regimes [M]:
- Across k unverified prose handoffs with error rate q, survival decays as (1 - q)^k
- High-reuse production buses (N >> 1, high L_downstream) amortize upfront schema cost C_spec / N
- On N=1 prototypes, rigid specs lose to prose

2/2 Theoretical scope & limits:
- Closed-form inequalities are hand-derived stylized models [M] with zero firm RCTs or hardware wattmeters here (joules = null)
- Real schemas incur ongoing maintenance cost under requirement drift
- Handoff joules live in companion benchmarks
